chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him), who said:

The divorced woman performs Hajj during her waiting period. The appropriate interpretation of this report is to understand it as referring to the Hajj of Islam (obligatory), because in the Hajj of Islam there is no obedience to the husband required of her. Rather, she is not permitted to go out except with his permission, or if she is in a waiting period where he has granted permission, regarding the Hajj of voluntariness. This indicates that.
ai.seo_question: Does a divorced woman need her ex-husband's permission to perform Hajj during her waiting period?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction by interpreting the ruling as applying specifically to Hajj al-Islam (the obligatory pilgrimage), which is a personal duty (fard 'ayn) requiring no spousal consent, unlike voluntary Hajj. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic principle that obligatory acts of worship generally supersede the husband's right of permission (idhn) during the waiting period, ensuring the woman fulfills her primary religious obligation.
